51572657.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to biotinylated human DCAF1 (1038 to 1400 residues) expressed in baculovirus infected in Sf9 insect cells assessed as dissociation constant measured for 60 secs by SPR analysis

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods - Surface Plasmon: SPR studies were performed using a Biacore T200 (GE Health Sciences Inc.) at 20 °C. Biotinylated DCAF1 (1038–1400 aa) was captured onto two flow cells of a streptavidin-conjugated SA chip (according to manufacturer’s protocol) achieving 4000–7000 response units (RU), whereas another flow cell was left empty for reference subtraction. Biotinylated WDR5 was captured on another flow cell as a negative control protein. Compounds were dissolved in 100% DMSO (20 mM stock) and diluted to working concentrations in 100% DMSO before threefold serial dilutions prepared in buffer with DMSO. For SPR analysis, compounds were diluted in HBS-EP buffer (10 mM Heps pH 7.4, 150 mM NaCl, 3 mM EDTA, 0.05% Tween-20), giving a final concentration of 0.5 or 1% DMSO. Kinetic determination experiments were performed using single cycle kinetics with an injection time of 60 s, off time of 120 s, and flow rate of 75 μL/min. Kinetic curve fittings and Kd calculations were done with a 1:1 binding model and the Biacore T200 Evaluation software (GE Health Sciences Inc.).
original_paragraph.Figure 1 caption: Figure 1. Confirmation of Z1391232269 binding to the DCAF1 WDR domain by biophysical methods. (C) SPR confirmed its binding to DCAF1 with a Kd of 11.5 ± 4.2 μM. Experiments were performed in triplicate.
original_paragraph.Figure 2 caption: Figure 2. Biophysical characterization of compounds 3c and 3d. Binding of compound 3c and 3d to DCAF1 WD40 domain was assessed using (A) SPR (Kd values of 490 ± 90 nM for 3d and 13.5 ± 0.2 μM for 3c) and (B) DSF (ΔTm of 2.8 ± 0.05 and 3.8 ± 0.08 °C at 25 and 50 μM for 3d, respectively, and no stabilization effect for 3c even at 50 μM). Compound 3d was orthogonally confirmed by (C) ITC with a Kd value of 932 ± 150 nM. The chemical structure of 3d is shown. Experiments were performed in triplicate.
original_paragraph.Figure 4 caption: Figure 4. Biophysical characterization of compound 26e (OICR-8268) with the DCAF1 WDR domain.
